description: Reusable gateware cores by function (see data/functions.json). files are paths in the upstream repo at the commit pinned in .claude/memory/sources.tsv. usage_patterns feed scan_core_usage.py (-> data/core_usage.json). Researched 2026-09-28 by 5 agents from the clones, reviews and catalogue; every file path verified to exist.

cores.name: vga2dvid + tmds_encoder DVI/TMDS core (Mike Field / EMARD)
cores.license: MIT (vga2dvid.vhd, tmds_encoder.vhd headers, Copyright 2012 Mike Field); fake_differential.v BSD-style (EMARD, no repo LICENSE file)
cores.summary: Converts VGA-style RGB+HV+blank into 8b/10b TMDS-encoded DDR/SDR bitstreams for the GPDI port; fake_differential wraps ECP5 ODDRX1F for the 4 pseudo-differential pairs. Copied into dozens of repos in this collection.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Drop-in for GPDI: instantiate vga2dvid with fake_differential(C_ddr=1) at 25 MHz pixel clock x5 shift clock.
cores.tests: none found (top/top_vgatest.v is a synthesis smoke test, not self-checking)

cores.name: hdl4fpga TMDS encoder (video component library)
cores.license: MIT (LICENSE; file header confirms same permissive terms, Copyright 2015 Miguel Angel Sagreras)
cores.summary: Reusable TMDS 8b/10b encoder entity from the hdl4fpga component library; encoder logic only, no serializer, meant to be paired with a board PHY (hdl4fpga ships ECP5 PHY files elsewhere in library/).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Pair with an ECP5 ODDRX1F/ODDRX2F serializer to drive GPDI; VHDL-only, hdl4fpga's own build scripts assume Diamond but the entity itself is toolchain-neutral.

cores.name: HDMI TX with audio (danodus ecp5_hdmi_audio_video)
cores.license: MIT (LICENSE, Copyright 2026 Daniel Cliche / 2019 Sameer Puri)
cores.summary: Full HDMI TX stack with audio and info-frame packet insertion (clock regeneration, AVI/audio packets); ULX3S top-level wiring already provided in boards/ulx3s/.
cores.ulx3s_notes: boards/ulx3s/ulx3s_top.v + hdmi_pll*.v are ready-made for GPDI; pick the hdmi_pll variant matching your target resolution.

cores.name: my_hdmi_device TMDS encoder + video timing (chip_balls)
cores.summary: hdmi_device.v does 8b/10b TMDS encoding from an incoming VGA-style RGB+sync stream; chip_balls.v wires it to ECP5 ODDRX1F for GPDI output. Builds against ulx3s_v20.lpf at --85k.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Already has a ulx3s_v20.lpf and Makefile target (PROJ=chip_balls, --85k, CABGA381); pair with ecp5pll.sv (also in this repo) for the pixel/shift clocks.

cores.name: smoldvi small portable DVI core
cores.summary: Minimal DVI TX (~20 LUTs/lane TMDS encoder); timing/encode/gearbox logic is vendor-neutral per the author, only the final serialiser targets a specific FPGA's DDR output primitive.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Port smoldvi_serialiser.v/smoldvi_clock_driver.v from iCE40 SB_IO to ECP5 ODDRX2F/ECLKSYNCB; the rest is drop-in.

cores.name: sound2fft TMDS encoder + ECP5 DVI serializer
cores.summary: 8b/10b TMDS encoder plus an ECP5 ODDRX1F-based DVI serializer, part of a larger FFT+PDM-mic+HDMI pipeline built for an ECP5 25F board (iCEsugar-Pro).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Board is ECP5 25F like the ULX3S 25F variant; only GPDI pin remapping should be needed.
cores.tests: waveform-only tb: projects/02_hdmi_test/hdmi_test_tb.v (no PASS/FAIL assertions found for tmds specifically)

cores.name: Apple 1 VGA text-mode framebuffer core (vga/vram/font_rom)
cores.license: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE, root; core inherited unchanged from upstream alangarf/apple-one)
cores.summary: VGA timing generator driving a character-cell text framebuffer (vram.v) and 8x8 font ROM (font_rom.v); board-agnostic core wired to ULX3S GPDI via the sibling rtl/boards/ulx3s/vga2dvid.v.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Already targets ULX3S 25F (boards/ulx3s/yosys/, ulx3s_v20.lpf, prebuilt bitstream committed); feed vga.v output into rtl/boards/ulx3s/vga2dvid.v for GPDI.
cores.tests: iverilog tb, no self-checking pass/fail: tools/iverilog/vga_tb.v (run via run_vga_tb.sh, not `make`)

cores.name: 6845 CRTC reimplementation (Graphics Gremlin)
cores.summary: Cycle-accurate Motorola 6845 CRTC reimplementation with an ISA-bus register interface, generating MDA/CGA-style character-cell video timing (hsync/vsync/cursor); board-agnostic, no vendor primitives.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Replace the ISA-bus register shim with a simple MMIO/CPU interface; the timing-generator half is directly usable standalone.

cores.name: f32c VGA timing + hardware text-mode overlay
cores.license: MIT-style permissive header (vga.vhd: Copyright 2015 Davor Jadrijevic, LICENSE=BSD; VGA_textmode.vhd: Copyright 2015 Ken Jordan, MIT-text)
cores.summary: VGA timing generator (vga.vhd) plus a full color text-mode overlay with selectable font ROM and optional SRAM/SDRAM bitmap plane (VGA_textmode.vhd), designed for the f32c SoC bus.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Not self-contained: expects f32c's video_cache_d/videofifo signal conventions; proven on ULX3S 12F/25F/45F/85F via rtl/lattice/ulx3s/top/top_ulx3s_12f_xram_sdram_tv.vhd and siblings.

cores.name: MiST composite/RGB scandoubler (15kHz to VGA)
cores.license: GPL-3.0-or-later (file header, Copyright 2015 Till Harbaum, MiST project)
cores.summary: Converts 15.7kHz composite/RGB-timed video into standard 31.4kHz VGA timing; vendored from the MiST project into an iCE40 HX4K design but the file itself instantiates no vendor primitives.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Portable structural Verilog; should synthesize unchanged for ECP5 with no primitive porting.

cores.name: vga_core / vga_timing portable VGA generator (Black Mesa Labs)
cores.license: CERN-OHL v1.2 (file header, Copyright 2017 Kevin M. Hubbard / Black Mesa Labs)
cores.summary: Portable VGA timing generator (vga_timing.v) and test-pattern/framebuffer core (vga_core.v), originally written for Xilinx then ported to iCE40 without vendor primitives per the repo README.
cores.ulx3s_notes: No porting needed for this pair of files; only the separate DVI serializer stage (not included) is board-specific.

cores.name: VgaSyncGen SpinalHDL VGA timing generator
cores.summary: SpinalHDL VGA sync-timing generator and clock-cycle counter components, proven on ULX3S 85F (ulx3s/Makefile CHIP:=85k); reused unchanged in the author's vga_pong project.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Requires the SpinalHDL/Scala toolchain to elaborate to Verilog before synthesis; generator parameters cover standard VGA modes.

cores.name: f32c PAL composite video (CVBS) generator
cores.license: BSD-2-Clause (file header, Copyright 2013 Marko Zec / University of Zagreb)
cores.summary: Generates PAL composite video (luma/chroma/sync encoding) from RGB framebuffer pixel data for direct resistor-DAC output; wired into f32c's own ULX3S top (rtl/lattice/ulx3s/top/top_ulx3s_12f_xram_sdram_tv.vhd).
cores.ulx3s_notes: ULX3S has no dedicated composite DAC pin; needs a resistor-ladder DAC on spare GPIO exactly as f32c's own 12f_..._tv top does.

cores.name: MiST composite/RGB scandoubler (composite-video input side)
cores.license: GPL-3.0-or-later (file header, Copyright 2015 Till Harbaum, MiST project)
cores.summary: Converts 15.7kHz composite/RGB-timed video (the format retro cores generate internally) up to 31.4kHz VGA timing; complementary to composite generation rather than a PAL/NTSC generator itself. No other true composite-out generator besides f32c's cvbs.vhd was found in this collection.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Useful when a retro core's internal video is composite-timed and needs converting for HDMI/VGA display rather than driven out as analog PAL/NTSC.

cores.name: lcd_video / spi_display multi-panel SPI LCD driver
cores.license: BSD (file headers: "AUTHORS=EMARD,MMICKO and Lawrie Griffiths / LICENSE=BSD"; VHDL twin "AUTHOR=EMARD / LICENSE=BSD")
cores.summary: VGA-clocked-in, SPI-clocked-out display driver; swaps ST7789/SSD1331/SSD1351/SSD1306 panels via a selectable init byte-sequence .mem file, free-running or synced to hsync/vsync/blank.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Pick the matching *_linit*.mem for your panel/orientation; c_clk_spi_mhz up to 125 MHz for the ST7789 default parameters.

cores.name: bit-bang SPI LCD driver (Apollo 11 FPGA)
cores.summary: Small bit-banged SPI LCD driver, plain Verilog with no vendor primitives; built for an iCE40 HX8K AGC (Apollo Guidance Computer) replica board.
cores.ulx3s_notes: No porting needed for the SPI logic itself; only clock/reset wiring needs adapting to ULX3S.

cores.name: RasteriCEr SPI display controller
cores.license: GPL-3.0-or-later (LICENSE, repo root; per-file headers confirm GPLv3-or-later, Copyright 2021 ToNi3141)
cores.summary: Streams a rasterizer's pixel output to a small SPI LCD via a generic SPI-slave-to-parallel bridge (SPI_Slave.v) feeding DisplayControllerSpi.v; built for an iCE40 UP5K board but neither file instantiates vendor primitives.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Portable logic; verify clock-domain assumptions before reuse on ECP5.

cores.name: Silice OLED drivers (ST7789/SSD1351/SSD1331)
cores.license: MIT (per-file header, "MIT license, see LICENSE_MIT in Silice repo root")
cores.summary: Silice `algorithm oled(...)` SPI display drivers for three common OLED controllers, part of Silice's ULX3S board framework and used across several Silice projects (oled_test, oled_sdcard_test, doomchip).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Requires the Silice compiler (compiles to Verilog); proven on ULX3S via Silice's own board support.

cores.name: SlabBoy ST7789 SpinalHDL LCD driver
cores.summary: SpinalHDL SPI driver component for an ST7789 LCD, part of the SlabBoy Game Boy core (idcode 12F, ULX3S-class ECP5 board).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Requires the SpinalHDL/Scala toolchain to elaborate to Verilog; check its bus/register interface against your design.

cores.name: SSD1322 OLED framebuffer driver (m68k-ulx3s)
cores.license: none found (no repo-level LICENSE; only the vendored lib/fx68k CPU core has its own separate LICENSE)
cores.summary: SSD1322 grayscale OLED driver: on reset runs the panel init sequence, then continually copies the framebuffer to the display via a small SPI-like tx sub-module (oled_tx).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Proven on ULX3S 85F (Makefile DEVICE=85k); targets SSD1322 rather than ST7789/SSDxxx1/1331 — adapt init bytes for other panels.

cores.name: ESP32 SPI OSD + spirw_slave ROM/disk loading stack
cores.license: osd.v and spi_osd.v: none found; spirw_slave_v.v: BSD ("AUTHOR=EMARD")
cores.summary: Intercepts the video stream to draw a text OSD window (osd.v) driven by an SPI slave register interface (spi_osd.v) that the ESP32 writes into; a generic SPI RW slave (spirw_slave_v.v) is what the ESP32-side MicroPython (osd.py) uses to browse/select ROMs on SD and push them into FPGA BRAM.
cores.ulx3s_notes: The de-facto ESP32<->FPGA OSD/loader stack, reused nearly verbatim across nes_ecp5, trs_80, apple2fpga, msx, sega-sms, sg_1000, ql, gamegear, vic_20; wire spi_osd into the video pipeline and spirw_slave_v to a SPI-mapped BRAM/register block.

cores.name: esp32_spi_gamepad minimal ESP32 SPI state receiver
cores.summary: Minimal SPI receiver decoding ESP32-side Bluetooth-gamepad button/axis state into FPGA registers; a smaller alternative pattern to the full OSD stack for simple ESP32->FPGA control-word links (no video overlay).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Good template for any small ESP32->FPGA state link that doesn't need the OSD video overlay machinery.

cores.name: esp32ecp5 MicroPython FPGA loader package
cores.summary: ESP32-side MicroPython package for loading ECP5 bitstreams over SPI (ecp5.py), a micro-FTP server for pushing files to ESP32 flash/SD (uftpd.py), and raw SD block read/write (sdraw.py) — the ESP32 half of the ULX3S ESP32<->FPGA loading path.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Runs on the ULX3S's onboard ESP32; pairs with an FPGA-side SPI slave (e.g. spirw_slave_v.v) to receive the loaded data.

cores.name: SPI RAM slave (ESP32 <-> FPGA memory-mapped link)
cores.summary: Presents FPGA BRAM as a Microchip-23K-style SPI RAM device to the ESP32 — an alternative transport (memory-mapped SPI RAM rather than the OSD register protocol) for ESP32-driven data/ROM loading.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Simpler than spirw_slave_v.v when the ESP32 only needs to fill/read a block of FPGA memory without an OSD protocol layer on top.

cores.name: OV7670 camera capture + SCCB config core
cores.summary: Captures OV7670 parallel PCLK/HREF/VSYNC/D[7:0] video into a FIFO with brightness/contrast controls, alongside a combined I2C/SCCB master (i2c_top.v, no external pull-ups needed) for camera register configuration; part of a full OV7670->Sobel->SDRAM->HDMI pipeline proven on ULX3S 85F.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Needs an OV7670 PMOD/breakout wired to GPIO; requires driving cmos_xclk and tuning the i2c_top SCCB timing per camera revision.

cores.name: camera85 nMigen OV7670 capture + image pipeline
cores.summary: nMigen OV7670 capture (camera.py), SCCB register bus (sccb.py) and camera register table (ov7670_config.py), part of a larger image-processing chain (ROI/statistics/gamma/color control) selectable to any ULX3S FPGA size at build time.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Requires the nMigen/amaranth-boards toolchain; camconfig.py + camread.py glue the pieces together.

cores.name: ImgController + ImgI2CMaster image-sensor interface (iCE40)
cores.license: public domain (LICENSE.md, one line, no SPDX id)
cores.summary: Image-sensor (parallel-bus) capture controller with an accompanying I2C master for sensor register configuration; uses iCE40 SB_IO primitives for the pixel-bus and I2C pins.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Needs SB_IO instances ported to ECP5 TRELLIS_IO; logic/FSM is otherwise portable.

cores.name: OV7670 capture + SCCB master (ulx3s-experiments)
cores.summary: OV7670 capture core (ov7670_capture.v) with a dedicated SCCB master (sccb_master.v) plus an async-FIFO clock-domain-crossing stack, proven on ULX3S 85F via apio.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Comes with a matching vga_display.v/oled_video.v output stage in the same directory for a live preview.

cores.name: OV7670 RGB/YUV capture + color-filter + VGA preview (ULX3S apio)
cores.license: GPL-3.0-or-later (LICENSE.md, software); repo also carries CERN-OHL-S-2.0 for hardware/PCB design
cores.summary: OV7670 RGB/YUV capture with on-the-fly colour filtering and a live VGA preview; one of many near-identical board variants (ULX3S/Alhambra II/Nexys4) in this repo sharing the same capture core, this is the apio/ULX3S build.
cores.ulx3s_notes: apio.ini + ulx3s_v20.lpf (or ulx3s_v20_pmodcam.lpf.txt) targets ULX3S directly; the repo has sibling variants (sobel, color-centroid tracking) using the same capture files.

cores.name: hdl4fpga generation-generic SDRAM controller
cores.summary: Chip-table-driven SDR/DDR/DDR2/DDR3 controller; ULX3S apps (graphics, scopeio) instantiate it with chip_data="MT48LC16M16MA2-7E", the ULX3S's real SDR chip, paired with the ecp5_sdrphy gearbox PHY.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Use chip_data="MT48LC16M16MA2-7E"; only the SDR path applies. Needs hdo/base + sdrampkg package dependencies.

cores.name: c-elegans ULX3S SDRAM controller
cores.summary: Standalone ULX3S SDRAM controller derived from the hamsterworks DE0-Nano FSM design, built and simulated with an IS42S16160.v chip model specifically for the ULX3S board.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Direct ULX3S reference controller; repo has no LICENSE file, treat as all-rights-reserved unless clarified.

cores.name: f32c generic SDR SDRAM controller
cores.summary: Generic SDR SDRAM command sequencer with a C_ports-generic multi-port arbiter, no vendor primitives; used across all f32c ULX3S SoC targets (12F/25F/45F/85F).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Plain clk/reset + C_clk_freq generic; drop-in SDRAM controller for a new ULX3S design.

cores.name: KianV mt48lc16m16a2_ctrl SDRAM controller
cores.license: ISC-style (LICENSE.md, Hirosh Dabui, permissive notice matching ISC wording)
cores.summary: SDRAM controller for the MT48LC16M16A2 chip used by the Linux-capable KianV RISC-V SoC (85F default, 12k..um-85k targets); part of a maintained, actively used Linux-on-ULX3S project.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Designed for the exact SDR chip ULX3S ships with; check icache/dcache wiring in the same sdram/ directory if reusing the whole memory subsystem.

cores.name: Oberon SDRAM_16bit controller + cache
cores.summary: Next186-derived 16-bit SDRAM controller paired with a direct-mapped cache_controller.v, used by the Project Oberon RISC5 ULX3S build (85F trellis / 12F diamond).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Copyleft (LGPL-2.1+): fine to link against, modifications to the file itself must stay LGPL.

cores.name: sdram_pnru simplistic SDRAM controller
cores.summary: Simplistic public-domain SDR SDRAM controller for 4x4Mx16 chips (e.g. MT48LC16M16A2): one access per system access, all 4 banks kept open, distributed refresh; part of EMARD's ULX3S example library.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Smallest/simplest of the seven sdram/ variants in ulx3s-misc; good starting point when a full-featured controller is overkill.

cores.name: Lightweight DDR3 AXI4 memory controller (ECP5)
cores.summary: Complete AXI4 DDR3 controller (Ultra-Embedded.com) proven on OrangeCrab r0.2 (ECP5): JEDEC DFI sequencer + plain-IO PHY (no DQSBUFM/DELAYF hardware read-training). Not for stock ULX3S (SDR SDRAM only), only for ECP5 boards/add-ons with DDR3.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Demonstrated only at a conservative 24 MHz DDR clock; re-tune DQ_IN_DELAY_INIT/TPHY_RDLAT for production speed. Needs a full LPF rewrite for any other board's DDR3 pinout.
cores.tests: none found (no build script or testbench in this clone)

cores.name: UberDDR3 controller + ECP5 PHY
cores.summary: DDR3 controller with a dedicated ecp5_phy/ddr3_phy_ecp5.v PHY (fabric-clocked BB/DELAYG, no PLL in-file); wired into the 3driscv RV32IMA SoC's Wishbone DDR3 path via a Blarney (Core.hs) wrapper.
cores.ulx3s_notes: GPL-3.0 copyleft vs. the parent project's MIT; check compatibility before reuse. Has SymbiYosys formal proofs and icarus/vivado regression tests, unlike most other DDR3 options here.

cores.name: Hackaday badge QPI-PSRAM PHY + cache (ECP5-native)
cores.summary: Cleanly layered QPI-PSRAM stack for two interleaved Lyontek LY68L6400 8 MB QPI chips (16 MB total): only qspi_phy_2x_ecp5.v touches ECP5 DDR-IO primitives, qpimem_cache/arbiter/dma_rdr above it are portable logic. Ships on real 45F badge silicon.
cores.ulx3s_notes: ULX3S has no on-board QPI PSRAM; only useful pairing with a compatible add-on board. Runs at 48 MHz interleaved; new LPF and pin remap required either way.
cores.tests: self-checking iverilog testbenches: qpimem_cache_testbench.v, qpimem_iface_testbench.v, qpimem_interleave_testbench.v

cores.name: hbc portable HyperBus/HyperRAM controller
cores.license: MIT-style (embedded header, Gnarly Grey LLC 2017; no repo LICENSE/COPYING file)
cores.summary: Self-contained HyperBus/HyperRAM controller in plain Verilog with no vendor primitives in the core FSM (hbc.v); written for iCE40 UP5K boards but architecturally the most portable HyperRAM core in the collection.
cores.ulx3s_notes: No ULX3S/ECP5 target exists; needs a new top-level with ECP5 tristate DQ IO and timing closure at the board's clock.
cores.tests: self-checking testbench: sim/hbc_tb.v ($display PASS/FAIL per byte)

cores.name: hyper_xface HyperRAM DWORD interface
cores.license: CERN-OHL-1.2 (claimed in-file header only, Kevin M. Hubbard 2018; not formalized at repo level)
cores.summary: DWORD-granularity HyperRAM interface (targets Cypress S27KL0641), optimized for RTL portability over bandwidth; DRAM clock is fabric-clock/4. Vendored into the pifive-cpu SoC but its instance is commented out there.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Portable Verilog-2001, no vendor primitives; needs its own top-level pin mapping and has not been exercised end-to-end in the parent project (instantiation commented out).

cores.name: no2fpga HyperRAM controller (no2hyperbus)
cores.summary: Wishbone-facing HyperRAM controller from Sylvain Munaut's no2fpga library: hbus_memctrl.v and hbus_dline.v are primitive-free link-layer logic, only hbus_phy_ice40.v instantiates iCE40 SB_IO for the physical DQ/RWDS pins.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Only hbus_phy_ice40.v needs an ECP5 rewrite (TRELLIS_IO/ODDRX1F in place of SB_IO); memctrl/dline logic is vendor-neutral as-is.
cores.tests: sim/hbus_memctrl_tb.v against a bundled sim/s27kl0642.v behavioral model

cores.name: ZipCPU sdspi SPI-mode SD controller
cores.summary: Wishbone-B4 SPI-mode SD/MMC controller, no vendor primitives, ~60 SymbiYosys formal proofs. "Silicon proven" per the author. Maps directly onto the ULX3S sd_clk/sd_cmd/sd_d[0]/sd_d[3] pins (shared with the ESP32).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Wire o_sck->sd_clk, o_mosi->sd_cmd, i_miso<-sd_d[0], o_cs_n->sd_d[3] per ulx3s_v20.lpf; ESP32 firmware must release these pins first.
cores.tests: formal (SymbiYosys, ~60 proofs in bench/formal/); Verilator/Icarus models in bench/cpp, bench/verilog

cores.name: MiSTer sd_card.sv (Harbaum/Sorgelig)
cores.summary: The well-known MiSTer-framework SD-card core (WIDE/OCTAL parameters), vendored as part of the ao486-derived PC-SoC peripheral set; not yet wired into the ULX3S probe top in this repo (CPU-only today).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Widely used and battle-tested across the MiSTer ecosystem; LGPL-3.0+ copyleft on modifications to the file itself.

cores.name: sd_controller (Searle/Edwards derived) SD reader
cores.license: custom permissive (Grant Searle acknowledgement clause: free to use, must credit, must not charge)
cores.summary: Single-block SD read/write stream controller adapted from Steven Merrifield's design via the Apple II emulator (Stephen Edwards) and Grant Searle's Z80 boards; used to load CP/M disk images on the ULX3S CP/M-Z80 build.
cores.ulx3s_notes: License requires attribution to Grant Searle and forbids charging for the file; simple enough to read/port in an afternoon.

cores.name: SDKarte SD card reader
cores.summary: Standalone SD card reader feeding a FIFO for a ULX3S MP3/audio jukebox project (song selection via buttons); small, single-purpose block.
cores.ulx3s_notes: No license header; treat as all-rights-reserved until clarified with the author before reuse.

cores.name: Silice sdcard SPI controller
cores.summary: SDHC/SDXC-only SD controller written in Silice, kept in slow-transfer mode throughout; author reports it tested working at 25, 50 and 100 MHz. Part of the ULX3S-supporting Silice board framework.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Requires the Silice compiler (yosys+nextpnr-ecp5 backend, GPL-3.0) rather than being usable as plain Verilog/VHDL.

cores.name: spimemio SPI/QSPI flash XIP controller
cores.summary: Memory-mapped SPI-flash execute-in-place controller from PicoSoC: no vendor primitives, expects four bidirectional flash_io[0:3] pins split into oe/do/di triples. Widely reused, well-tested reference XIP controller.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Needs a board-side tristate wrapper (ECP5 generic inout/BB instead of the reference tops' iCE40 SB_IO) for the shared ULX3S config-flash pins.
cores.tests: root Makefile self-checking testbenches (test/test_wb/test_synth/...) exercise picosoc including spimemio via firmware; no standalone spimemio testbench found

cores.name: MappedSPIFlash read-only XIP driver
cores.summary: Minimal read-only SPI-flash-in-memory-space driver from Bruno Levy's FemtoRV32 project, vendored to run the FemtoRV32 core on the ULX3S 85F longwave-SDR design.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Read-only (no write/erase); smallest option here when a design only needs to execute firmware from flash.

cores.name: NEORV32 ULX3S XIP flash-execute top
cores.summary: ULX3S 85F board top pairing the NEORV32 RISC-V core's built-in XIP module with the ECP5 config-flash pins (USRMCLK), so firmware executes directly from SPI flash instead of block RAM.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Built via a dedicated Makefile.xip target; simplest path to XIP-from-flash on ULX3S if already using NEORV32.

cores.name: qspi_phy_ecp5 QSPI flash PHY (ECP5-native)
cores.summary: ECP5-native QSPI flash PHY (drives USRMCLK and the shared config-flash IO through TRELLIS_IO/IFS1P3DX/OFS1P3DX) used by the PicoRV32-based USB DFU bootloader that ships bitstreams into ULX3S flash from the US2 port.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Proven in production on ULX3S (emard's DFU bootloader, 1d50:614b); pairs with picorv32/picosoc for a full XIP+DFU stack.

cores.name: Wishbone Quad-SPI flash controller (Gisselquist-derived)
cores.summary: ZipCPU/Gisselquist eqspiflash core (originally for the Arty board) wrapped as a Wishbone slave (wbqspiflash), ported into EMARD's ULX3S example library with read/write/erase register control and XIP support.
cores.ulx3s_notes: GPL-3.0 copyleft; has a bench/busmaster.v simulation harness for standalone verification before wiring into a SoC.

cores.name: wbuart Wishbone UART
cores.summary: Wishbone-mapped 8N1 UART: separate tx/rx byte engines plus FIFOs behind a wbuart register-file wrapper. Built for the pifive-cpu SoC on ULX3S 85F.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Proven on ULX3S 85F via fpga/ulx3s/Makefile (yosys+nextpnr-ecp5+ecppack); wire wbuart into any Wishbone SoC.

cores.name: f32c sio serial I/O
cores.summary: f32c SoC's UART peripheral, memory-mapped, used across many f32c ULX3S/ECP5 boards for the boot loader console.
cores.ulx3s_notes: VHDL, no vendor primitives; f32c's own build is Diamond-only but this file is portable to an open ghdl-yosys flow.

cores.name: SAO UART phy (minimal 8N1)
cores.summary: Minimal byte-oriented 8N1 UART interface used by the ULX3S example SoC's ESP32 SAO sideband link.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Actually instantiated in ulx3s__hazard3's example_soc.v build for ULX3S 85F/ULX4M-LD; simplest place to start for a tiny UART.

cores.name: Solderpad uart_tx (Tom Verbeure)
cores.license: Solderpad Hardware License v0.51 (file header, Copyright 2018 Tom Verbeure)
cores.summary: Simple UART transmitter copied across several lawrie ULX3S example/retro-computer repos alongside the PS/2 examples.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Weak-reciprocal license (Solderpad), not pure permissive; check terms before closed-source reuse.

cores.name: verilog-uart tx/rx
cores.summary: Small dedicated, board-independent UART tx/rx pair with a well-specified README (exact baud error, framing/noise handling).
cores.ulx3s_notes: ulx3s.lpf present but no committed build script; drop the two files into a project and instantiate directly.
cores.tests: tb/receiver_tb.v, tb/transmitter_tb.v (iverilog, self-checking status not confirmed)

cores.name: APB SPI master (microSD)
cores.summary: Small software-driven APB SPI master (mode 0, MSB-first, no FIFO/DMA) built for the ULX3S micro-SD socket.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Actually wired into ulx3s__hazard3's example_soc for ULX3S 85F; CLKDIV register sets SCLK from clk/2*(CLKDIV+1).

cores.name: glasgow SPI controller (Amaranth)
cores.summary: Pure-Amaranth SPI controller core, part of Glasgow's gateware library; elaborates to plain Verilog with no vendor primitives.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Needs an Amaranth build flow (glasgow CLI / YoWASP toolchain) to elaborate; ECP5 platform support already exists in the repo.
cores.tests: software/tests (cocotb-style, not spi.py-specific in this pass)

cores.name: llsdspi low-level SPI engine
cores.summary: Portable low-level SPI-mode engine (originally for SD cards) plus a byte/command-level sdspi wrapper; vendor-neutral, no synthesis flow bundled.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Heaviest formal verification of any SPI core in the collection (~60 SymbiYosys proofs); GPL-3.0 copyleft.
cores.tests: bench/formal/*.sby SymbiYosys proofs; bench/cpp verilator C++ tb (self-checking)

cores.name: SPI master (Bus Pirate NextGen Ultra)
cores.summary: Configurable SPI master written for the Bus Pirate NextGen Ultra debug probe; no vendor primitives in the file itself.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Repo builds for iCE40 HX8K, but spimaster.v has no SB_* instantiation, so it drops onto ECP5 unmodified.
cores.tests: components/spi has a standalone testbench, not wired into hdl/Makefile

cores.name: verilog-i2c (alexforencich)
cores.summary: Well-known alexforencich I2C master/slave IP with ready-made Wishbone and AXI-Lite register wrappers and an init sequencer.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Vendored as a git submodule in a repo whose fpga/ulx3s/Makefile targets ULX3S 85F (yosys+nextpnr-ecp5+ecppack); pick the wbs_8/16 wrapper for a Wishbone SoC.

cores.name: BeagleWire i2c-master
cores.license: GPL-2.0 (repo LICENSE; note pcf header claims gplv3, inconsistent)
cores.summary: Self-contained I2C master for the BeagleWire cape, using two SB_IO instances for the open-drain SDA/SCL pads.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Replace the two SB_IO tristate instances with ECP5 BB/TRISTATE_IO primitives; the FSM logic itself is portable.

cores.name: glasgow I2C core (Amaranth)
cores.summary: Pure-Amaranth I2C controller/target gateware; part of Glasgow's actively maintained protocol library.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Needs the Amaranth/glasgow build flow; ECP5 platform support already present (rev D board).

cores.name: SAO I2C command engine
cores.summary: Low-level I2C command engine with open-drain SDA/SCL controls, driving the ULX3S example SoC's SAO bridge.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Actually built into ulx3s__hazard3's example_soc for ULX3S 85F; board-level wrapper supplies the tri-state I/O.

cores.name: no2usb-derived ECP5 USB FS device core (had2019 bootloader)
cores.summary: Early ECP5-ported snapshot of Sylvain Munaut's no2usb: full-speed USB device MAC/PHY (EP buffers, CRC, transaction engine) driving the US2 pins directly; the core shipped as the fielded ULX3S DFU bootloader's USB device.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Runs at 48 MHz from a 25->48MHz EHXPLLL (sysmgr.v); wire to usb_fpga_bd_dp/dn + usb_fpga_pu_dp on US2.
cores.tests: waveform-only (cores/usb/sim/*_tb.v via iverilog, never run to a pass/fail check)

cores.name: circuit-killer USB FS serial device (VHDL, ULX3S-built)
cores.summary: USB CDC-ACM device core with its own soft PHY (usb11_phy_vhdl, no vendor primitives) plus an optional ULPI wrapper; the repo ships ULX3S v2.0/v3.1.7 LPFs and 12F/25F/45F/85F build dirs.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Use usb11_phy_vhdl (direct US2 pins), not ulpi_wrapper (needs an external ULPI PHY chip).

cores.name: f32c USB CDC-ACM device + soft PHY
cores.license: BSD-2-Clause (repo fallback, no per-file header on usb_serial.vhd); usb11_phy is OpenCores-permissive (Copyright 2000-2002 Rudolf Usselmann)
cores.summary: USB 2.0 CDC-ACM device entity (usb_serial.vhd) over a UTMI-style soft PHY (usb11_phy, ported from Verilog), wired into f32c SoCs proven across ULX3S 12F-85F.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Same core family as emard__ulx3s-misc/examples/usb/usbcdc; check docs/projects/f32c__f32c.md before reuse (license per-file uncertainty).

cores.name: hdl4fpga USB 1.1 device core
cores.summary: Portable USB 1.1 device core with no vendor primitives, switchable device/host role via a build constant; used on real ULX3S hardware by boards/ULX3S/apps/ser_debug.vhd on the US2 pins.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Set the usb_device constant true in a ser_debug.vhd-style top; needs the matching usbphy.vhd PHY.
cores.tests: waveform tb in boards/ULX3S/testbenches (12 tb files across boards, not all self-checking)

cores.name: ulixxe USB CDC-ACM device core
cores.summary: Self-contained full-speed USB CDC-ACM device (SIE, control/bulk endpoints, PHY rx/tx) with no BRAM/vendor primitives, shipped with pin files for 21 boards (Fomu, TinyFPGA-BX, iCEBreaker...).
cores.ulx3s_notes: No ULX3S pin file yet; add one for usb_fpga_bd_dp/dn + pull-up, following an existing board example.

cores.name: ulx3s-misc USB CDC-ACM device (VHDL)
cores.summary: Same usb_serial.vhd device entity family as f32c, packaged as a standalone ULX3S example with a Windows .inf driver file; this copy documents itself as GPL, unlike the BSD-2 fallback claimed for the f32c copy.
cores.ulx3s_notes: examples/usb/usbcdc/usbtest.vhd is the ready-to-build ULX3S top.

cores.name: Ultra-Embedded USB FS host (ulx3s-misc copy)
cores.language: Verilog, VHDL (usbh_sie_vhdl.vhd, usbh_host_hid.vhd variants also present)
cores.summary: Ultra-Embedded's full-speed USB host SIE plus a HID-report host driver; the most reused USB-host core in the collection, copied into emard's NES/Apple-1/Minimig/Next186/Papilio-Arcade/Phoenix/Apple2fpga cores for keyboard/gamepad input.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Drop-in on ULX3S US2 pins; pair with a report_decoder for the target gamepad/keyboard (see emard__nes_ecp5/usb/report_decoder).

cores.name: circuit-killer minimal USB HID host
cores.summary: Minimal single-file USB HID host state machine with CRC5/CRC16 helper functions, built for ULX3S 45F/85F (saitek/dragonrise-oled projects) with dedicated OLED demo tops.
cores.ulx3s_notes: No license file: get owner clearance before reuse.

cores.name: emard standalone USB1.1 host PHY/SIE (usb_host repo)
cores.summary: Standalone USB1.1 host PHY + SIE + register block, packaged as its own small ULX3S 12F demo with a BRAM firmware loader (ucmem/), separate from the ulx3s-misc/nes_ecp5 usbh_sie lineage.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Demo bitstream targets ULX3S 12F (soc/build.sh --12k).

cores.name: emard USB host + gamepad report decoders
cores.summary: Same usbh_sie host core as the ulx3s-misc copy, plus five ready HID report decoders for specific gamepads (NES-style, Saitek, Darfon, Xbox 360), the piece usually missing when reusing the bare host core.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Use report_decoder/usbh_report_decoder_xbox360.v (or another pad's file) to parse usbh_host_hid's output into button state.

cores.name: hdl4fpga USB 1.1 host core
cores.summary: Portable USB 1.1 host core, no vendor primitives, sharing a PHY with the device core (usbdev.vhd) via a build-time role switch; used on real ULX3S hardware in boards/ULX3S/apps/ser_debug.vhd.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Set usb_device=false to select host mode in a ser_debug-style top.

cores.name: ULX3S/ULX4M USB DFU bootloader (had2019-playground)
cores.license: per file: bootloader RTL BSD-3-Clause, USB core + DFU firmware LGPL-3.0-or-later, picorv32.v ISC (see docs/DFUs.md)
cores.summary: The gateware ULX3S/ULX4M ship from flash address 0: PicoRV32 + no2usb-derived USB device core enumerating as DFU 1d50:614b, writing the user bitstream to flash 0x200000 via a QSPI master, with a 6-zone alt-setting layout. Fully documented in docs/DFUs.md.
cores.ulx3s_notes: USER_BITSTREAM_ADDR, dfu_zones[0] (fw/usb_dfu.c) and ecpmulti --address must all agree; PROGRAMN (LPF site M4) must loop back for hand-off.
cores.tests: none found (cores/usb/sim + project tbs are waveform-only, never run to a pass/fail check)

cores.name: Hazard3-Doom vendored DFU bootloader (ULX4M-LD validated)
cores.license: provenance in LICENSES/HAD2019-Bootloader-NOTICE.md; per-file licenses match the emard original (BSD-3/LGPL-3.0+/ISC)
cores.summary: Self-contained fork of the had2019 bootloader (own mk/, cores/, no external Makefile deps), remapped buttons, validated on real ULX4M-LD v0.0.3 (LFE5UM-85F) hardware, with a byte-for-byte readback recovery procedure documented in README_ULX4M_BOOTLOADER.md.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Prefer this copy over the emard original for a self-contained tree; same USER_BITSTREAM_ADDR/dfu_zones agreement rule applies.
cores.tests: none found (same iverilog-compile-only sim rule as the original)

cores.name: no2usb DFU runtime + dfu_helper.v (iCE40)
cores.summary: Button debouncer that reboots into the no2bootloader DFU image via SB_WARMBOOT (long press) or resets the app (short press); the DFU class firmware itself (usb_dfu.c/usb_dfu_rt.c) lives in the fetched no2usb submodule.
cores.ulx3s_notes: iCE40-only (SB_WARMBOOT multiboot); porting to ECP5 needs a different warm-boot mechanism plus the no2bootloader project, which is not in this collection.

cores.name: mii_ipoe ARP/IP/UDP/DHCP stack
cores.summary: Full MII-level protocol stack (eth_rx/tx, ARP, IPv4, UDP, ICMP, DHCP client) built from library/mii/*.vhd, generic RMII/MII pad-independent.
cores.ulx3s_notes: This is the exact stack behind emard__ulx3s-bin's prebuilt DHCP+ping-responder bitstream on the ULX3S LAN8720 RMII PHY (GP/GN 9-13); pair with ulx3s-misc's examples/eth/rmii for the board-side pad wiring. Repo toolchain is Diamond-only, but this file has no vendor primitives.

cores.name: Gigabit RGMII MAC
cores.summary: Complete Gigabit Ethernet MAC with RGMII PHY interface, AXI-Stream data ports and PTP timestamp triggers.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Built for a Colorlight i9 (LFE5U-45F); rgmii_tx.v genuinely instantiates ECP5 ODDRX1F, but rgmii_rx.v uses behavioral posedge/negedge sampling rather than a real IDDRX1F (comment says so explicitly) — verify RX timing before reuse.

cores.name: MDIO Clause-22 management controller
cores.summary: IEEE 802.3 Clause-22 MDIO read/write controller plus a paged wrapper for 88E1512-style PHY register maps.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Built for a Lattice Versa ECP5-5G board (SGMII/RGMII bring-up demo); the MDIO logic itself is board-agnostic and reusable for any PHY needing register access over MDIO.
cores.tests: sim/ has 1 iverilog tb file, not confirmed MDIO-specific

cores.name: RMII hex-dump packet sniffer
cores.summary: Self-contained single-file RMII receiver that hex-dumps captured LAN8720 packets to OLED/DVI; includes an ARP-reply memory skeleton, not a full MAC.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Documents the exact ULX3S LAN8720 RMII pinout (gn9/gp10/gn10/gp13 TX, gp11/gn11/gp12/gn12 RX, gn13 MDIO) referenced by other RMII cores in this collection.

cores.name: ps2_intf keyboard decoder
cores.summary: Input-only PS/2 keyboard interface: clock filtering, 11-bit frame shift-in, byte-valid strobe. The most widely-copied PS/2 core in the collection.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Same file copied verbatim into hoglet67__ice40beeb, hoglet67__ice40atom, lawrie__ulx3s_bbc_micro, lawrie__ulx3s_acorn_atom, lawrie__blackicemxbook, lawrie__verilog_examples.
cores.tests: ps2/ps2_test.v exists but is waveform-only, no PASS/FAIL

cores.name: f32c ps2 VHDL core
cores.summary: PS/2 keyboard/mouse interface entity used in the f32c SoC library.
cores.ulx3s_notes: VHDL, no vendor primitives; pair with f32c's own SoC memory map or lift standalone.

cores.name: ps2_port bidirectional PS/2
cores.summary: Bidirectional PS/2 port (adds host-to-device writes, e.g. keyboard LEDs) built on the same ps2_intf lineage.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Use when a design needs to set keyboard LEDs or otherwise talk back on the PS/2 bus, not just decode input.

cores.name: ps2kbd + ps2mouse (EMARD)
cores.license: BSD (ps2kbd.v header: AUTHOR=Paul Ruiz, LICENSE=BSD); ps2mouse.v: none found
cores.summary: Separate keyboard decoder and a full 3-byte PS/2 mouse controller with automatic power-up initialization.
cores.ulx3s_notes: ps2kbd.v reused in stuij__odyssey and danodus__xgsoc; ps2mouse.v reused in danodus__xgsoc and the emard/linuxjedi minimig_ecs forks.

cores.name: OpenCores JTAG TAP + JTAGG bridge
cores.license: LGPL-2.1-or-later (jtag_slave.v OpenCores tap_top.v header, Igor Mohor/Nathan Yawn); top_jtagg_slave.v: none found
cores.summary: Generic OpenCores JTAG TAP (jtag_slave.v, vendor-neutral) plus a demo top that bridges it through the ECP5 JTAGG primitive so user logic gets its own JTAG chain via the board's existing FTDI/ESP32 JTAG.
cores.ulx3s_notes: top_jtagg_slave.v is a real ULX3S example (clk_25mhz, btn/led/oled/gpdi ports); ODDRX1F instances are only in the demo's DVI/OLED wiring, not the TAP itself.

cores.name: ECP5 JTAGG demo (Ecp5JtagDemo)
cores.summary: Minimal, well-documented instantiation of the ECP5 JTAGG primitive with a reverse-engineering write-up of its TCK/TDI/TDO timing.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Built for a Colorlight i5 (ECP5-25F); pin remap only needed to reuse on ULX3S.
cores.tests: tb/ iverilog testbench, waveform-only ($dumpvars, no PASS/FAIL)

cores.name: eSPI bus capture + packet decoder
cores.license: none found (repo-wide; only ecp5pll.sv credited BSD to EMARD)
cores.summary: eSPI (Enhanced SPI) bus signal capture with CDC double-registering and single/dual/quad IO decode, plus a packet decoder pipeline.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Nix-flake reproducible ULX3S build (default 12F, also 25/45/85); a purpose-built protocol logic analyzer, not a generic one.

cores.name: OpenDAP SW-DP + Mem-AP (SWD debug probe)
cores.summary: ADIv5.2 SW-DP (Serial Wire Debug) and APB Mem-AP implementation: an alternative to JTAG for debugging soft cores.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Repo's own README calls the SoC experimental ("no idea how to program it"); the DP/Mem-AP cores themselves are standalone and CC0.

cores.name: SUMP logic analyzer core (ECP5-ported)
cores.summary: Classic openbench SUMP-protocol logic analyzer (sampler, RLE encoder, trigger, BRAM ring buffer) already re-targeted to ECP5 via ecp5_pll.v (an SB_PLL40_CORE version, pll.v, also exists for iCE40).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Built --25k with an idcode for 12F in this repo; BRAM-based capture buffer, not SDRAM-backed.

cores.name: wb_intercon Wishbone mux/arbiter (olofk)
cores.summary: Standard olofk/wb_intercon Wishbone crossbar mux and round-robin arbiter, wired into tenyr's own CPU SoC.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Fetched as a git submodule; actually used in hw/verilog/top.v for a ULX3S 12F build (yosys+nextpnr-ecp5+ecppack).

cores.name: AHB-Lite crossbar/arbiter/APB bridge
cores.summary: AHB-Lite crossbar, arbiter, splitter and an AHB-Lite-to-APB bridge, connecting the Hazard3 CPU to its peripherals.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Actually instantiated in example_soc/soc/example_soc.v for the ULX3S 85F / ULX4M-LD build; fetched via the Hazard3-libfpga submodule.
cores.tests: no unit test of the crossbar/arbiter themselves; indirectly exercised by test/sim SoC-level cxxrtl tests (coremark, riscv-tests)

cores.name: wb_intercon (olofk), iCE40 copy
cores.summary: Same olofk/wb_intercon library as kulp__tenyr, vendored directly (not a submodule) alongside a VexRiscv SoC.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Files contain no SB_* primitives; only the board's PCF/PLL needs porting, the bus logic is vendor-neutral.

cores.name: MAX1112x ADC reader (ulx3s-misc)
cores.summary: Init+read core for the onboard MAX1112x (MAX11125-family) SPI ADC used on the ULX3S; shift and array register variants.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Drop-in for the ULX3S onboard MAX11125 ADC pins; verified in docs/projects/emard__ulx3s-misc.md.
cores.tests: none found (repo-wide: only examples/audio/testbench/sinewave.c is a non-HDL C reference model)

cores.name: Digital down-converter + AM/FM demod chain (post-ADC)
cores.license: none found (no LICENSE file in repo)
cores.summary: Digital down-converter, tuner NCO, AM/FM demodulators plus CIC decimator and FIR filter, fed from an external fast ADC on OrangeCrab 25F; no vendor primitives seen.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Needs an external high-speed ADC on ULX3S (no onboard equivalent); the DSP chain itself (CIC/FIR/demod) is portable.

cores.name: MAX1112x ADC reader (ulx3s-emi copy)
cores.summary: Same EMARD MAX1112x ADC init/read core vendored into the ulx3s-emi (12F) example board design.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Same core as ulx3s-misc; use if you want the ulx3s-emi top-level wiring as a starting point.

cores.name: SPI ADC core (Bus Pirate Ultra HDL)
cores.summary: Standalone 14-bit SPI ADC read/calibration core for the Bus Pirate Ultra's onboard ADC channel.
cores.ulx3s_notes: adc.v itself is plain Verilog (no SB_* seen); the board's pll.v/buspirate.v use iCE40 SB_PLL40_CORE/SB_IO and would need ECP5 equivalents if reused wholesale.

cores.name: Sigma-delta PCM audio DAC (fpga-dac)
cores.summary: First-order sigma-delta stereo audio DAC that streams 48kHz 16-bit signed PCM from SPI flash; simple phase accumulator, no vendor primitives in audio.v itself.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Self-contained modulator (l_pwm_acc/r_pwm_acc); reuse just the sigma-delta block and drive it from any PCM source (SDRAM, ESP32, etc.) instead of SPI flash. rtl/pll.v is board-specific and needs re-deriving for 25 MHz ULX3S input.

cores.name: PDM audio DAC (hadbadge2019 soc/audio)
cores.summary: First-order pulse-density-modulation DAC core with dither, used for the hadbadge2019 SoC's audio synth output.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Pairs well with soc/audio/synth_core.v in the same repo; plain Verilog, no ECP5-specific primitives.

cores.name: Resistor+PWM hybrid DAC (dacpwm)
cores.license: none found (no header in file; repo has no LICENSE file)
cores.summary: Combines a coarse resistor-ladder DAC (upper bits) with a PWM output (lower bits) to raise effective DAC resolution from a small pin count.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Parametric C_pcm_bits/C_dac_bits; used in the ULX3S audio example (examples/audio/hdl/top_audio.v) with 25 MHz clock.
cores.tests: waveform-only (examples/audio/testbench/sinewave.c is a plain C reference model, not a Verilog tb)

cores.name: Sigma-delta DAC (synthowheel)
cores.summary: Standalone sigma-delta modulator used to drive the audio output of the synthowheel ULX3S synth project.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Pairs with synth.vhd in the same repo; single-bit output suitable for a simple RC lowpass to line-out.

cores.name: Sigma-delta DAC (up5k-demos)
cores.license: none found (repo has no LICENSE/COPYING file; nes.v claims GPL but no license text present)
cores.summary: Tiny parametric-width sigma-delta DAC (delta/sigma adder pair) used for the NES APU audio output.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Plain Verilog, no SB_* primitives; drops onto ECP5 unchanged, only the surrounding NES top-level is iCE40-specific.

cores.name: I2S audio interface (ulx3s-misc)
cores.summary: Parametric I2S transmit core (fmt/clk_hz/lrck_hz generics) demonstrated in the ULX3S audio example, VHDL wrapper over a Verilog core.
cores.ulx3s_notes: clk_hz=25000000 matches the ULX3S board oscillator; see examples/audio/hdl/top_audio.v for a complete instantiation.
cores.tests: waveform-only (testbench/sinewave.c is a non-HDL C reference model)

cores.name: I2S receiver (orangecrab-usb)
cores.license: none found (repo has no LICENSE/COPYING file)
cores.summary: Small I2S receiver: deserializes left/right 32-bit channel data from an external I2S codec given a 64fs input clock.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Plain Verilog, portable; pairs with hdl/clkdiv/clkdiv.v in the same repo for MCLK/BCLK generation.

cores.name: I2S RX/TX + PDM/CIC mic front-end (sound2fft)
cores.summary: I2S receiver/transmitter plus a PDM-microphone CIC decimator and PDM modulator, part of a cocotb bit-exact-tested audio+FFT+HDMI pipeline for iCESugar-Pro (ECP5 25F).
cores.ulx3s_notes: Portable front-end; only the TMDS serializer elsewhere in the repo needs ECP5 ODDRX1F, not these audio blocks.
cores.tests: cocotb, bit-exact vs numpy (per repo README; test scripts not individually re-verified here)

cores.name: S/PDIF transmitter (f32c)
cores.license: BSD-2-Clause (repo-level per docs/projects/f32c__f32c.md; file itself carries no SPDX header, same ackspace.nl/EMARD-derived source)
cores.summary: Same ackspace.nl-derived S/PDIF transmitter as synthowheel's, vendored into the f32c SoC's peripheral set.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Used from the f32c SoC's audio/CPU bus glue; can be lifted standalone like the synthowheel copy.

cores.name: S/PDIF transmitter (synthowheel)
cores.summary: S/PDIF biphase-mark transmitter, derived from the ackspace.nl SPDIF project with EMARD's clock-divider modification; 24-bit signed PCM in, 25 MHz/48 kHz defaults.
cores.ulx3s_notes: C_clk_freq=25000000 matches the ULX3S oscillator directly; single-bit spdif_out needs a coax/TOSLINK line driver off-board.

cores.name: SN76489 PSG (sound chip)
cores.license: none found (no header in file; repo has no LICENSE/COPYING)
cores.summary: Texas Instruments SN76489 programmable sound generator (3 tone channels + noise), the Sega Master System/BBC Micro PSG; parametric AUDIO_RES output width.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Proven on ULX3S 85F in lawrie__ulx3s_sms, cheyao__sega-sms and danodus__ulx3s_sms; feed audio_out into an I2S/DAC block from this same collection.

cores.name: JT51 (YM2151 FM synth core)
cores.summary: Jotego's cycle-accurate reimplementation of the Yamaha YM2151 FM synthesizer (used in many arcade boards incl. CPS1); ships its own `ver/` verification testbenches.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Used as the CPS1 music core over a LiteX SoC targeting ULX3S (radiona_ulx3s.py); GPL-3.0 copyleft applies.
cores.tests: ver/ directory with per-module testbenches (jotego JT-series standard test harness; not individually re-run here)

cores.name: JT89 (AY-3-8910-like PSG)
cores.summary: Jotego's AY-3-8910-compatible 3-channel PSG core (tone/noise/volume/mixer), used as the sound chip in the Atari ST-style ULX3S 68000 project.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Proven on ULX3S 85F alongside src/fx68k.sv (68000 core) in the same repo.

cores.name: SID (MOS 6581/8580) reimplementation, technology-independent
cores.license: CERN-OHL-S-2.0 (LICENSE, root; matching header in gateware/*.sv, Dag Lem 2022-2023)
cores.summary: Reference-quality Commodore 64 SID sound chip DSP core (waveform/envelope/filter/voice/DAC), technology-independent with no SB_* primitives in the listed files.
cores.ulx3s_notes: Core logic ports directly to ECP5; needs an I2S/sigma-delta output stage from this collection and the surrounding reDIP-SID board glue rewritten.

cores.name: SID reimplementation (icesid)
